answer_explanation: Regarding EP-A, the period for paying the additional search fee is two months and the fees must be paid at the latest by 22 April 2013 [11 February 2013 + 10 days (=21 February 2013) + 2 months (=21 April 2013), extended to Monday 22 April 2013], Rule 64(1) EPC, Rule 126(2) EPC, Rule 131(4) EPC and Rule 134(1) EPC. Regarding PCT-B, the period for paying the additional fee is one month and the fees must be paid at the latest on 11 March 2013, Rule 40.1(ii) PCT and Rule 80.2 PCT. The PCT provisions do not have the so-called "10-day-rule".

question_text: Company X intends to file in its own name a European patent application EP-II claiming  priority from an earlier European patent application EP-I. EP-I was filed on  29 February 2012 and it claims no earlier priority.

answer_choices.1: The priority period expires on 1 March 2013.
answer_choices.2: The priority declaration must be made at the latest by 1 July 2013.
answer_choices.3: In order to validly claim priority, EP-II must be in respect of the same invention as EP-I.
answer_choices.4: Company X can validly claim priority from EP-I only if it was the applicant of EP-I at the date of filing. Legal questions

answer_explanation: The priority period expires on 28 February 2013 [29 February 2012 + 12 months (=28 February 2013)], Article 87(1) EPC and Rule 131(4) EPC. The priority declaration must be made at the latest by 1 July 2013 [29 February 2012 + 16 months (=29 June 2013), extended to Monday 1 July 2013], Rule 52(2) EPC, Rule 131(4) EPC and Rule 134(1) EPC. In order to validly claim priority, EP-II must be in respect of the same invention as EP-I, Article 87(1) EPC. According to the same provision, not only the applicant of EP-I can validly claim priority from EP-I: the successor in title as well as any person to whom the right to claim priority from EP-I was validly transferred can validly claim priority from EP-I.

question_text: European patent application EP-P was a first filing filed in 2009. EP-P itself is not a  European divisional application. You received the first communication under  Article 94(3) EPC for EP-P in December 2011. EP-P was refused with a decision dated  6 February 2013. Today, 25 February 2013, you intend to file EP-D as a European  divisional application of EP-P.

answer_choices.1: EP-D must be filed with the European Patent Office in Berlin, Munich or The Hague.
answer_choices.2: Renewal fees in respect of EP-P already due today shall also be paid for EP-D.
answer_choices.3: You must first file an appeal against the decision to refuse EP-P before you can validly file EP-D.
answer_choices.4: The language of the proceedings of EP-P and EP-D must be the same. Legal questions

answer_explanation: The European divisional application EP-D must be filed with the European Patent Office in Berlin, Munich or The Hague (Rule 36(2) EPC, third sentence, as entered into force on 1 April 2010). Irrespective of whether EP-P was filed in an official language of the EPO or in another language, the language of the proceedings of EP-P and EP-D has to be the same (Rule 36(2) EPC, first and second sentence, as entered into force on 1 April 2010). Renewal fees were already due for EP-P for at least the third and fourth year: these renewal fees are also due for EP-D, Rule 51(3) EPC. In view of decision G1/09, in the case where no appeal is filed, a European patent application which has been refused by a decision of an Examining division is still pending within the meaning of Rule 36(1) EPC during the period for filing a notice of appeal. Thus, it is not necessary to file an appeal to render the application pending so as to validly file a European divisional application. The twenty-four months time limit –triggered by the first communication under Article 94(3) EPC in respect of EP-P according to Rule 36(1)(a) EPC as entered    - 3 - into force on 26 October 2010– for filing a divisional application to EP-P is still running.

question_text: In January 2009, the international application PCT-1 was filed in Japanese at the  Japanese Patent Office. A translation of PCT-1 into English was provided upon entry  into the European phase. In the examination phase before the EPO, the applicant notes  that a term of the description was incorrectly translated into English. The applicant now  requests the correction of this translation error.

answer_choices.1: The correction can only be made if it is immediately evident from the English translation as filed upon entry into the European phase.
answer_choices.2: The correction can be made if it has a basis in the Japanese text as originally filed at the Japanese Patent Office.
answer_choices.3: A wrongly translated term in a European patent application can always be replaced by the correct term given in the priority document.
answer_choices.4: The correction cannot be made because PCT-1 was not filed in an official language of a Contracting State of the European Patent Organisation. Legal questions

answer_explanation: The provisions of Article 14(2) EPC, second sentence, apply also to Euro-PCT applications in view of Article 153(2) EPC. The applicant of PCT-1 may bring the English translation into conformity with the application documents of the international application PCT-1 as originally filed. In this context it is irrelevant whether the correction is immediately evident from the English translation. Corrections cannot be derived from the priority document, Guidelines, H-VI, 4.2.1. (The provisions of Rule 56(3) EPC do not apply here.)

question_text: The mention of the grant of a European patent EP-X was published on 16 May 2012. A  Portuguese citizen resident in Portugal filed a notice of opposition by fax on  15 February 2013 to the EPO, explaining why the subject-matter claimed in EP-X was  not inventive in view of two published patents D1 and D2 explicitly identified in the fax.  The fax was entirely written in Portuguese. The opposition fee was paid on the same  day. Today, 25 February 2013, a letter from the Portuguese citizen that was sent three  days ago reaches the EPO. Annexed to the letter is:  (a) a complete translation in English of the fax sent on 15 February 2013,  (b) copies of the two prior art documents D1 and D2.

answer_choices.1: The opposition is not admissible, as the copies of the two prior art documents were filed after expiry of the opposition period.
answer_choices.2: The notice of opposition could have been filed at the latest on 18 February 2013.
answer_choices.3: The translation was filed within the prescribed time limit.
answer_choices.4: The opposition is not validly filed, as the Portuguese citizen should have appointed a professional representative for filing the opposition. Legal questions

answer_explanation: To file an admissible opposition, it is not required to file copies of D1 and D2 together with the notice of opposition, Rule 83 EPC (see also Guidelines D-IV 1.2.2.1 (v), last two paragraphs). An opposition against patent EP-X could have been filed at the latest on 18 February 2012 [16 May 2012 + 9 months (=16 February 2013), extended to Monday, 18 February 2013], Article 99(1) EPC, Rule 131(4) EPC and Rule 134(1) EPC. The translation of the notice of opposition shall be filed within one month of filing the notice of opposition: therefore it was filed in time, Article 14(4) EPC and Rule 6(2) EPC. The Portuguese citizen resident in Portugal need not be represented in opposition proceedings, Article 133(2) EPC.

question_text: The international application PCT-Q claims priority from an earlier US-application, US-P.  Upon entry into the European phase before the EPO, the claims of PCT-Q were  replaced by a modified set of claims R. After receiving the supplementary European  search report from the EPO, a further modified single independent claim S was filed in  January 2013.

answer_choices.1: ... the priority document US-P.
answer_choices.2: ... the set of modified claims R.
answer_choices.3: ... the abstract of PCT-Q.
answer_choices.4: ... one claim of PCT-Q having the same wording as claim S.  Legal questions

answer_explanation: Amendments to PCT-Q must be based on the application documents as originally filed, Article 123(2) EPC: It is not allowable to add matter only present in the priority document (Guidelines, H-IV, 2.3.5), in the abstract (Article 85 EPC) or in a set of claim modified in the course of the proceedings.

question_text: The mention of the grant of European patent EP-G was published in July 2012. The  patent proprietor of EP-G is Mr. G. EP-G was filed without claiming priority in  January 2009. Your client, Mr. O, wants the patent to be revoked. He thinks that claim 1  of EP-G is unclear. In fact, there are two possible interpretations of claim 1. Product Z,  which has been on the market since November 2008, falls under one of the two  interpretations.

answer_choices.1: ... lack of clarity is not a valid ground for opposition.
answer_choices.2: ... if product Z was put on the market by Mr. G, product Z does not form part of the state of the art.
answer_choices.3: ... EP-G should be opposed for lack of novelty, explaining in the notice of opposition why product Z anticipates the subject-matter of claim 1 of EP-G.
answer_choices.4: ... product Z does not form part of the state of the art, as it is not a pre-published written document. Legal questions

answer_explanation: Lack of clarity is not a valid ground for opposition, Article 100 EPC. Everything made available to the public, for instance by use or by selling, before the date of filing of EP-G constitutes state of the art within the meaning of Article 54(2) EPC for EP-G. It is irrelevant who put product Z on the market. A possible way to have patent EP-G revoked is to oppose it for lack of novelty using product Z as prior art.

question_text: European patent application EP-Y was refused at oral proceedings before the examining  division. The oral proceedings took place on 28 January 2013. Today,  25 February 2013, you received the written reasoned decision.

answer_choices.1: A notice of appeal against the decision to refuse the patent application must be filed at the latest by 28 March 2013.
answer_choices.2: The statement setting out the grounds of appeal and possibly amendments must be filed together with the notice of appeal.
answer_choices.3: The examining division shall rectify its decision if it finds the appeal to be admissible and well-founded.
answer_choices.4: The appeal fee is always reimbursed, if the board of appeal sets aside the decision of the examining division. Claim analysis

answer_explanation: The appealable decision is the written reasoned decision received on 25 February 2013, Rule 111(2) EPC: the period of two months for filing an appeal is computed from the notification of the decision and not from the announcement of the decision at oral proceedings. Following the provisions of Article 108 EPC, the statement setting out the grounds of appeal or possibly amendments may be filed after the notice of appeal but within four months of the notification of the decision. The examining division shall rectify its decision if it finds the appeal to be admissible and well-founded, Article 109(1) EPC. If the board of appeal sets aside the decision of the examining division, reimbursement of appeal fees occurs only if it is equitable in view of a substantial procedural violation, Rule 103(1)a) EPC.

answer_choices.1: During opposition proceedings, an amendment to a European patent introducing subject-matter which was present only in the priority document but not in the European patent application as filed is allowable under Article 123(2) EPC.
answer_choices.2: Intermediate generalisations are never allowable under Article 123(2) EPC.
answer_choices.3: An amendment introducing subject-matter which was present only in the abstract of the application is allowable under Article 123(2) EPC.
answer_choices.4: An amendment introducing subject-matter which was present only in the claims filed in reply to a communication under Rule 58 EPC in conjunction with Rule 57(c) EPC is allowable under Article 123(2) EPC. Legal questions 2018/P/EN/3

answer_explanation: Under Article 123(2) EPC, it is not allowable to add matter to a European patent present only in the priority document for that patent, Guidelines, H-IV 2.2.5. [Note that there is an exception under Rule 56(3) EPC]. Intermediate generalisations may be allowable under specific circumstances, see Guidelines, H-V 3.2.1. The abstract may not be taken into account for any purpose other than for technical information, Article 85 EPC. Subject-matter present only in claims filed after the date of filing (as is the case for claims filed in reply to a communication under Rule 58 in conjunction with Rule 57(c) EPC) goes beyond the subject-matter of the application as filed (description and drawings), see also Guidelines, H-IV 2.2.3.

question_text: Daniela is resident in Poland. On 13 February 2018, Daniela filed the European patent  application EP-D as a first filing. The EPO noticed that the drawings mentioned in the  description were evidently missing. With a communication dated 22 February 2018, the  EPO invited Daniela to file the missing drawings.

answer_choices.1: If Daniela ignores the invitation, EP-D will be deemed to be withdrawn.
answer_choices.2: If Daniela files the missing drawings on 3 May 2018, EP-D will receive 3 May 2018 as its date of filing.
answer_choices.3: Daniela may validly file the missing drawings for EP-D on 6 June 2018, provided she pays the fee for further processing.
answer_choices.4: If an applicant is not invited by the EPO to file missing parts of the description or missing drawings, he may validly file them within two months of the date of filing. Legal questions 2018/P/EN/4

answer_explanation: If Daniela ignores the invitation, then any reference to the drawings will be deemed to be deleted, Rule 56(4)(a) EPC (the legal consequence is not that the application is deemed to be withdrawn). If the missing drawings are filed within two months of the notification of that communication [22 February + 10 days (4 March 2018) + 2 months], i.e. 4 May 2018 (Rule 56(1) EPC, Rule 126(2) EPC, Rule 131(4) EPC) the application shall be re-dated to the date on which the missing drawings were filed, Rule 56(2) EPC. According to Rule 135(2) EPC, further processing is ruled out in respect of the period under Rule 56(2) EPC. An applicant may file missing parts of the description or Page 1 of 18 missing drawings of his own motion within two months of the date of filing, Rule 56(2) EPC and Guidelines, A-II 5.2.

question_text: The European patent application EP-A was filed on 29 February 2016. EP-A claims  priority from an earlier patent application filed in March 2015. The mention of the grant of  a European patent based on EP-A was published in April 2017. An opposition against  this patent was validly filed in January 2018. The only ground for opposition raised by  the opponent is lack of novelty according to Article 100(a) EPC. The only document cited  is the French patent application FR-B published in July 2015 and filed in January 2014.  In the notice of opposition, the opponent argues that the priority claimed in EP-A is not  valid.

answer_choices.1: The validity of the priority right as such is not a ground for opposition under Article 100 EPC.
answer_choices.2: FR-B is state of the art under Article 54(2) EPC if the priority of EP-A is not valid.
answer_choices.3: If the priority of EP-A is valid, then FR-B belongs to the state of the art under Article 54(3) EPC in view of its earlier filing date.
answer_choices.4: If the opponent raises today, 26 February 2018, an objection of lack of sufficiency of disclosure against EP-A, then this is a fresh ground for opposition. Legal questions 2018/P/EN/5

answer_explanation: The validity of the priority right as such is not a ground for opposition, since it is not mentioned in Article 100 EPC. If the priority of EP-A is not valid, then the effective date of EP-A in accordance with Article 89 EPC is the filing date of EP-A (29 February 2016). In such a case, FR-B is state of the art according to Article 54(2) EPC, and it can be used to attack novelty (and inventive step) of EP-A. The national application FR-B can only be prior art under Article 54(2) EPC and not under Article 54(3) EPC. Lack of novelty and lack of sufficiency of disclosure are separate grounds for opposition, Article 100 EPC. Moreover, the objection of lack of sufficiency of disclosure was raised after the expiration of the opposition period (see G10/91 and Guidelines, D-V, 2.2). Thus, the objection of lack of sufficiency is considered to be a fresh ground for opposition.

question_text: The Mexican applicant Juana wishes to enter the European phase with the international  application PCT-J today, 26 February 2018. Juana is resident in Mexico. PCT-J was  filed in Spanish in August 2015, without claiming any priority. PCT-J was published in  Spanish.

answer_choices.1: A translation of PCT-J must be filed with the EPO within two months from entry into the European phase.
answer_choices.2: If a translation of PCT-J is not filed in due time, a valid option is to request further processing.
answer_choices.3: In proceedings before the EPO Juana must be represented by a professional representative.
answer_choices.4: Juana is entitled to a reduction of the examination fee. Legal questions 2018/P/EN/8

answer_explanation: Where no priority is claimed, the translation of an international application has to be supplied within thirty-one months from the date of filing, i.e. sometime in March 2018. If the translation is not filed in due time, the European patent application is deemed to be withdrawn (Rule 160(1) and (2) EPC), and further processing can be requested, Article 121(1) EPC and Rule 135(1) EPC. In proceedings before the EPO, Juana must be represented by a professional representative, Article 133(2) EPC. Juana is not entitled to a reduction of the examination fee, since she is neither resident in nor a national of a contracting state of the EPC, Rule 6(4) EPC and Article 14(4) EPC.

question_text: The mention of the grant of European patent EP-X was published in July 2017. The  single claim of EP-X is directed to a product. The patent was validated in Germany and  Italy. The date of filing of EP-X is 1 March 2014.

answer_choices.1: Any infringement of European patent EP-X can be dealt with under the EPC and by the EPO, provided that opposition proceedings are pending.
answer_choices.2: The patent proprietor is entitled under all circumstances to produce in Germany any matter that is covered by the claim of EP-X.
answer_choices.3: The patent proprietor is entitled under all circumstances to sell in Italy any matter that is covered by the claim of EP-X.
answer_choices.4: The renewal fees for European patent EP-X that are due in 2018 cannot be validly paid to the EPO. Legal questions 2018/P/EN/9

answer_explanation: Any infringement of a European patent is dealt with by national law, Article 64(3) EPC. A patent gives the patent proprietor the right to exclude third parties from using the protected invention: it does not automatically allow the patent proprietor to produce and sell matter that is protected by the patent. The obligation to pay renewal fees to the EPO terminates in 2017, with the payment of the renewal fee due in respect of the year in which the mention of the grant of the European patent is published in the European Patent Bulletin, Article 86(2) EPC.

question_text: The international application PCT-M was filed in August 2015 without claiming priority.  PCT-M was searched by the EPO as the International Searching Authority in  February 2016. The International Searching Authority raised non-unity objections with  respect to the subject-matter of claims 20 to 35. The applicant did not pay any additional  fees. The International Searching Authority issued a partial search report covering  claims 1-19. PCT-M entered the European phase today, 26 February 2018, and is  referred to in the following as Euro-PCT-M. No amendments have been filed.

answer_choices.1: The applicant will have an opportunity to amend the claims of Euro-PCT-M, before substantive examination of Euro-PCT-M begins.
answer_choices.2: If in the application documents which are to serve as the basis of the examination of Euro-PCT-M an invention is claimed that was not searched by the EPO as the International Searching Authority, the applicant will be invited to pay a further search fee in respect of this invention.
answer_choices.3: If the applicant does not pay claims fees today, 26 February 2018, Euro-PCT-M will be deemed to be withdrawn.
answer_choices.4: If the applicant does not comment today, 26 February 2018, on the written opinion of the International Searching Authority, Euro-PCT-M will be deemed to be withdrawn. Legal questions 2018/P/EN/10

answer_explanation: The EPO has acted as the International Searching Authority. The EPO will, among others, invite the applicant to amend the description and claims in accordance with Rule 161(1) EPC soon after Euro-PCT-M enters the European phase. Any amendment or comment can be filed within six months of that communication. If in the application documents which are to serve as the basis of the examination an invention is claimed that was not searched by the EPO as the International Searching authority, the applicant will be invited to pay further search fees in respect of any such invention, Rule 164(2)(a) EPC. The present set of claims includes at present 35 claims, and therefore claims fees are due in accordance with Rule 162(1) EPC: however, the legal consequence of not paying claims fees for some claims is that these claims shall be deemed to be abandoned, Rule 162 (4) EPC. The application is not   Page 5 of 18 deemed to be withdrawn, if the applicant fails to comment today, since he may do so within the period set in accordance with Rule 161(1) EPC.

question_text: A notice of appeal was validly filed on 1 February 2018 against the decision to refuse the  European patent application EP-B. The decision is dated 6 December 2017. According  to the decision, claim 1 of the sole request is not novel over D1 and is not inventive over  D2 in combination with the common general knowledge of the skilled person. The  statement setting out the grounds of appeal has not yet been filed.

answer_choices.1: The statement setting out the grounds for the appeal must be filed at the latest on 6 April 2018.
answer_choices.2: On 31 January 2018 EP-B was pending.
answer_choices.3: The examining division will grant interlocutory revision, if the applicant files an auxiliary request which is clearly allowable, novel and inventive.
answer_choices.4: The examining division will grant interlocutory revision, if the applicant can convince the examining division that claim 1 of the sole request is novel over D1. Legal questions 2018/P/EN/11

answer_explanation: The statement setting out the grounds for the appeal must be filed at the latest on 16 April 2018 [6 December 2017 + 10 days (Rule 126(2) EPC) + 4 months (Article 108 EPC and Rule 131(4) EPC) = 16 April 2018]. An application is pending if it was refused and if no appeal has yet been filed until the expiry of the time limit for filing the notice of appeal [6 December 2017 + 10 days (Rule 126(2) EPC) + 2 months (Article 108 EPC and Rule 131(4) EPC) = 16 February 2018], see also G1/09. An interlocutory revision is never possible on the basis of an auxiliary request, even if it would overcome the grounds for refusal, Guidelines, E-XI, 7.4.3. If interlocutory revision is to be granted, the applicant must address convincingly all grounds for refusal, i.e. novelty over D1 and inventive step over D2.

question_text: The applicant of EP-S has been summoned to oral proceedings on 23 March 2018. The  final date for making written submissions was 23 February 2018. On 23 February 2018,  the applicant filed amended claims 1-9, that replace claims 1-10 previously on file. The  amended claims 1-9 change the focus of the discussion and raise completely new  issues. The applicant also informed the examining division that he will not attend the oral  proceedings.

answer_choices.1: The examining division performs today, 26 February 2018, an additional search and refuses today EP-S on the basis of a document found during this search.
answer_choices.2: The examining division does not admit amended claims 1-9 into the proceedings because the request is late filed under Rule 116 EPC.
answer_choices.3: The examining division holds oral proceedings for EP-S in the absence of the applicant.
answer_choices.4: The oral proceedings for EP-S are held by an examining division consisting of only one technically qualified examiner. Claim analysis 2018/P/EN/12

answer_explanation: A decision (such as a decision to refuse a patent application) may not be based on facts and evidence (such as a new document) on which the applicant did not have the opportunity to be heard, Article 113(1) EPC and Page 6 of 18 G4/92. The examining division can exercise the discretion not to admit requests filed during prosecution of the application, such as after summons to oral proceedings have been issued. However, the discretion is exercised under Rule 137(3) EPC (see also Guidelines, H-II, 2.7.1), since the time frame for filing amendments in respect of EP-S under Rule 116(1) and (2) EPC was still open. The examining division may hold oral proceedings in the absence of the party duly summoned, Rule 115(2) EPC. The examining division has three technically qualified examiners, Article 18(2) EPC.

question_text: An inventor resident in San Marino validly filed a European patent application last week.  He is considering appointing the professional representative before the EPO Mr. A to  help him prosecute the application.

answer_choices.1: In this case, the inventor does not need to be represented by a professional representative before the EPO.
answer_choices.2: In this case, in order to be validly represented by Mr. A, a signed authorisation must be filed with the EPO.
answer_choices.3: If the inventor, after validly appointing Mr. A, wants to appoint a different professional representative before the EPO, Mr. B, from another association, then Mr. B need not provide a signed authorisation, if Mr. A informs the EPO of the change of representative.
answer_choices.4: For a change of attorney to be validly registered by the EPO, an administrative fee has to be paid. Legal questions

answer_explanation: An inventor resident in a Contracting State is not obliged to be represented by a professional representative before the EPO, Article 133(1) and (2) EPC. San Marino is a Contracting State since 1 July 2009. In order to be validly represented by a professional representative, it is not required to file a signed authorisation: the principle of self- appointment applies for the first representative (in this case Mr. A). A second representative (in this case Mr. B) need not file a signed authorisation, if the European Patent Office is notified (by Mr. A) that the previous representative's authorisation has terminated, Article 1(1) and (2) of the Decision of the President of the EPO dated 12 July 2007, Special edition No. 3, OJ EPO 2007, L.1. There is no provision for the payment of an administrative fee for the registration of a change of attorney.

question_text: A communication under Article 94(3) EPC is dated 15 January 2015. In the  communication a time limit of four months is set for replying to objections raised by the  examining division.

answer_choices.1: The communication is deemed to be delivered on Monday, 26 January 2015, because 25 January 2015 falls on a Sunday.
answer_choices.2: Without resorting to a legal remedy, the reply to the communication must be filed with the EPO at the latest on 26 May 2015.
answer_choices.3: Further processing for replying to said communication can be validly requested at the latest on Monday, 27 July 2015.
answer_choices.4: An extension of the time limit for the reply can be validly requested on 20 May 2015.    Legal questions

answer_explanation: The communication is deemed to be delivered on 25 January 2015 [15 January 2015 + 10 days, Rule 126(2) EPC]. It is immaterial that the deemed delivery day falls on a Sunday. In order to avoid further processing and other prolongation of the proceedings, the reply to the communication must be filed at the latest on 26 May 2015 [25 January 2015 + 4 months (= 25 May 2015), extended to Tuesday 26 May 2015, Rule 131(4) EPC  and Rule 134(1) EPC)]. Note that on 25 May 2015 the EPO is closed. Further processing can be requested within a period of two months from the communication under Rule112 EPC concerning the loss of rights (Article 121(1) EPC and Rule 135(1) EPC). The communication is sent only after expiry of the time limit for replying to the communication under Article 94(3) EPC: 27 July 2015 is not the latest day for requesting further processing. The period for replying to the communication may be extended upon request, if the request is presented before the expiry of the period, Rule 132(2) EPC.

question_text: You filed an international application PCT-A on 21 February 2014 without claiming  priority. The EPO as the International Searching Authority considered that the  application did not comply with the requirement of unity of invention. The invention first  mentioned in the claims was searched. An invitation to pay one additional search fee  was sent to you. The invitation is dated 16 January 2015. You received the invitation on  19 January 2015.

answer_choices.1: The additional search fee can be validly paid on 26 February 2015.
answer_choices.2: Today, 23 February 2015, you can file an international application PCT-B validly claiming priority from PCT-A, wherein the claims of PCT-B are directed to the second invention.
answer_choices.3: A valid option would be to request a supplementary international search for the second invention of PCT-A to be carried out by the EPO.
answer_choices.4: According to the provisions of the PCT, the additional search fee is paid directly to the International Searching Authority.  Legal questions

answer_explanation: The additional search fee is payable within one month from the date of the invitation [16 January 2015 + 1 month (=16 February 2015), Rule 40(1)(ii) PCT and Rule 80.2 PCT]. There is no “ten day rule” for the delivery of communications under the PCT. Since the priority period expires only today, Monday 23 February 2015, you can still file today an international application PCT-B claiming priority from PCT-A [21 February 2014 + 12 months (= Saturday 21 February 2015), extended to 23 February 2013, Article 8(2)(a) PCT and Article 4 C (1) of the Stockholm Act of the Paris Convention for the protection of industrial property and Rule 80.5 (i) PCT]. The International Searching Authority (in this case the EPO) is not competent to carry out a supplementary international search (Rule 45bis.9 (b) PCT, see also Guidelines, E-VIII, 1 (vi)). The additional search fee is paid directly to the International Searching Authority, Rule 40.2 (b) PCT.

question_text: The mention of the grant of a European patent EP-Z was published on 18 June 2014.  The language of the proceedings of EP-Z was English. Mr. Kurz, a Czech citizen  resident in Slovakia, wishes to file an opposition against that patent. He intends to use  the European patent application EP-Y as a novelty destroying document. EP-Y was  published in German.

answer_choices.1: The notice of opposition must be filed at the latest on 18 March 2015.
answer_choices.2: Mr. Kurz is entitled to a reduction of the opposition fee, if he first files the opposition in Czech and then timely files a translation in English.
answer_choices.3: Mr. Kurz need not file a translation of EP-Y.
answer_choices.4: If Mr. Kurz wants to use the Slovak language during oral proceedings, it is sufficient to notify the EPO one month before the oral proceedings.  Legal questions

answer_explanation: The notice of opposition must be filed at the latest on 18 March 2015 [18 June 2014 + 9 months (= 18 March 2015), Article 99(1) EPC and Rule 131(4) EPC]. Mr. Kurz is entitled to file the notice of opposition in Czech or in Slovak (Rule 3(1) EPC and Article 14(4) EPC). However, according to Rule 6 EPC as entered into force on 1 April 2014, there is no longer any reduction of the opposition fee. Since the documentary evidence was filed in an official language of the EPO, the EPO will not require a translation, Rule 3(3) EPC. Any party may use an official language of a Contracting State during oral proceedings, but the party must then provide interpretation into the language of the proceedings, Rule 4(1) EPC.

question_text: Your client filed on 2 August 2012 an international application PCT-M without claiming  priority. According to the written opinion established by the EPO as the International  Searching Authority, the subject-matter of several claims of PCT-M lacks novelty.

answer_choices.1: In the present case, the latest date for entering the European phase without resorting to further processing was 2 February 2015.
answer_choices.2: If PCT-M enters the European phase on 27 March 2015, at least one further processing fee must be paid.
answer_choices.3: In view of the fact that the EPO considers that the subject-matter of several claims of PCT-M is not novel, it is mandatory to file amended claims on which the examination at the EPO is to be based.
answer_choices.4: One requirement for validly entering the European phase with PCT-M on 27 February 2015, is that a renewal fee must be paid.  Legal questions

answer_explanation: The latest date for entering the European phase is 2 March 2015 [2 August 2012 + 31 months (= 2 March 2015), Rule 159(1) EPC and Rule 131(4) EPC]. Entry into the European phase on 27 March 2015 is possible: however, at least one further processing fee is due, Article 121(1) EPC and Rule 135(1) EPC. The applicant is not obliged to file amended claims: he may file comments without filing amended claims, Rule 161(1) EPC. The renewal fee in respect of the third year for Euro-PCT-M has fallen due earlier, on 31 August 2014, Article 86(1) EPC and Rule 51(1) EPC. For PCT-M, one of the requirements for entry into the European phase on 27 February 2015 is the payment of the renewal fee in respect of the third year, Rule 159(1)(g) EPC and Guidelines, A-X, 5.2.4. [Note: For a request for early processing to be effective, the applicant must comply with the 2/10 requirements stipulated in Rule 159(1) EPC as if the 31-month time limit expired on the date the applicant requested early processing (see Notice from the European Patent Office dated 21 February 2013 concerning the request for early processing, OJ EPO 2013, 156).]

question_text: Your client filed in September 2012 an international application PCT-N without claiming  priority. PCT-N contains a drawing. Your client wants to enter the European phase and  he wants to file amended claims.

answer_choices.1: In order for an amendment to PCT-N to be allowable under Article 123(2) EPC, the amendment cannot relate to unsearched subject-matter.
answer_choices.2: An amendment which is allowable under Article 123(2) EPC may be novel and inventive over the disclosure of PCT-N as filed.
answer_choices.3: An amendment which is allowable under Article 123(2) EPC may be based on subject-matter found only in the drawing of PCT-N.
answer_choices.4: An amendment is allowable under Article 123(2) EPC if it is based on subject-matter found only in the claims amended under Article 19 PCT. Legal questions

answer_explanation: A European patent application may not be amended in such a way that it contains subject-matter which extends beyond the content of the application as filed, Article 123(2) EPC. An amendment may be allowable under Article 123(2) EPC although it is not based on searched subject-matter (thus offending for instance the requirements of Rule 137(5) EPC). If an amendment is novel and inventive over the application as filed, then it was not directly and unambiguously derivable from the application as filed. An allowable amendment may be based on a drawing, but never on subject-matter found only in amendments filed under Article 19 PCT: such amendments are filed after receiving the international search report, i.e. well after the filing of the application.

question_text: For questions 7 and 8 consider the following situation:    The German company C filed in December 2013 a German utility model application   DE-C directed to a solution of the substance X in water. The utility model was published  in March 2014.  In November 2014 company C filed a European patent application EP-C claiming priority  from DE-C. EP-C has three claims: claim 1 is directed to a solution of the substance X;  claim 2, which is dependent on claim 1, is directed to a solution of the substance X in  water; claim 3, which is dependent on claim 1, is directed to a solution of the  substance X in alcohol.  In September 2014, the solution of the substance X in water was made available to the  public in a scientific publication.  Company C has not filed any other applications.

answer_choices.1: It is possible to claim priority from utility model application DE-C for EP-C.
answer_choices.2: The effective date of claim 3 is the date of filing of EP-C.
answer_choices.3: If an independent claim is entitled to a priority date, then a claim depending from the independent claim must be entitled to the same priority date.
answer_choices.4: The first filing for a solution of the substance X in alcohol is EP-C. Legal questions

answer_explanation: Priority can be claimed from a utility model, Article 87(1) EPC. Claim 3 is not entitled to priority, since this invention was not disclosed in DE-C: the first filing for a solution of the substance X in alcohol is EP-C. If the priority for an independent claim is valid, no conclusion can be drawn on the validity of the priority of a thereof depending claim.

question_text: QUESTION 8

answer_choices.1: Claim 2 of EP-C lacks novelty with respect to the scientific publication.
answer_choices.2: The scientific publication is state of the art under Article 54(2) EPC for claim 1 of EP-C.
answer_choices.3: DE-C is state of the art under Article 54(2) EPC for claim 3 of EP-C.
answer_choices.4: Claim 3 of EP-C lacks novelty with respect to the scientific publication   Legal questions

answer_explanation: Claims 1 and 3 have as their effective date the date of filing of EP-C, Article 87(1) EPC. Consequently, the scientific publication is state of the art under Article 54(2) EPC for these two claims. Claim 2 is entitled to the priority date of DE-C: the scientific publication is not state of the art for claim 2. Claim 3 is novel over the scientific publication, since water and alcohol are different solvents.

question_text: A European patent application EP-R was filed in December 2013 without claiming  priority. The search division stated in the search opinion that the invention described in  EP-R is not sufficiently disclosed. In the description of the invention of EP-R, reference  is made to a co-pending European patent application EP-Q. EP-Q was filed with the  EPO in October 2013.

answer_choices.1: The skilled person has the same level of skill for assessing inventive step and sufficient disclosure.
answer_choices.2: The finding of the search division with respect to lack of sufficiency of disclosure of EP-R cannot be contested in examination proceedings before the EPO.
answer_choices.3: The skilled person may use common general knowledge to carry out the invention.
answer_choices.4: A condition for taking EP-Q into account in the assessment of sufficiency of disclosure is that EP-Q was made available to the public no later than on the publication date of EP-R.  Legal questions

answer_explanation: The applicant can contest the finding of the search division, e.g. in the response to the European search report, Rule 70a(1) EPC. The skilled person has the same level of skill for assessing inventive step and sufficient disclosure, (Guidelines, G-VII, 3, last sentence) and he may use common general knowledge to carry out the invention. EP-Q can be considered for assessing sufficiency of disclosure, only if the document was made available to the public no later than on the date of publication of EP-R (Guidelines, F-III, 1, 5.2 and 8 and H-IV, 2.3.1).

question_text: The mention of the grant of European patent EP-X was published in September 2014.  The patent proprietor is company CE and Ms Smith is mentioned as the inventor.  Ms Smith is a former employee of company CE. She left company CE in  November 2014 after a dispute. Ms Smith is resident in Great Britain.

answer_choices.1: Ms Smith can validly file an opposition against EP-X, although she is mentioned as the inventor.
answer_choices.2: A candidate preparing for the European qualifying examination who is resident in the EU can validly file an opposition in his own name against EP-X, for training purposes.
answer_choices.3: Ms Smith can validly file an appeal against the decision to grant EP-X.
answer_choices.4: The professional representative before the EPO Mr Singer can validly file an opposition in his own name on behalf of Ms Smith and without naming Ms Smith as the opponent.  Claim analysis

answer_explanation: Any person may give notice of opposition, provided he or she is not the patent proprietor. The inventor Ms Smith, the candidate preparing for the EQE and Mr Singer can therefore oppose EP-X (Article 99(1) EPC and G 9/93). In the case of Mr Singer filing the opposition for Ms Smith, there is no circumvention of the law within the meaning of G 3/97. The motivation for filing an opposition is irrelevant. Appeal proceedings are only open to parties to proceedings (Article 107 EPC).

question_text: Giorgio validly filed an Italian patent application IT-G as a first filing. IT-G discloses a  frame made of metal, preferably aluminium, for device X. IT-G was filed in April 2016  and withdrawn in May 2016. In September 2016, a frame made of steel for device X was  made available to the public in a catalogue. Today, 6 March 2017, Giorgio files a  European patent application EP-G claiming priority from IT-G. Claim 1 of EP-G is  directed to a frame made of metal for device X. Claim 2 of EP-G is directed to a frame  made of steel for device X. Claim 3 of EP-G is directed to a frame made of aluminium for  device X. Claim 4 of EP-G is directed to a frame made of copper for device X.

answer_choices.1: The catalogue is state of the art under Article 54(2) EPC for claim 1 of EP-G.
answer_choices.2: The catalogue is state of the art under Article 54(2) EPC for claim 2 of EP-G.
answer_choices.3: The catalogue is state of the art under Article 54(2) EPC for claim 3 of EP-G.
answer_choices.4: The catalogue is state of the art under Article 54(2) EPC for claim 4 of EP-G.  Legal questions 2017/P/EN/3

answer_explanation: EP-G was filed within 12 months from the filing of IT-G, Article 87(1) EPC. Only claims 1 and 3 of EP-G are directed to the same invention as IT-G (frame made of metal and frame made of aluminium), Article 87(1) EPC and G2/98. The withdrawal of the priority application IT-G has no effect on its validity, Article 87(3) EPC. IT-G is the first filing. The priority for claims 1 and 3 being valid, the effective date under Article 89 EPC for these two claims is the filing date of IT-G. Therefore, the catalogue is not prior art within the meaning of Article 54(2) EPC for claims 1 and 3. However, the effective date of the subject-matter of claims 2 and 4 is the date of filing of EP-G (frame made of steel and frame made of copper were not disclosed in IT-G), Article 89 EPC. Thus, the catalogue is prior art under Article 54(2) EPC for these two claims.

question_text: Jill filed the international application PCT-J on 4 August 2014 without claiming a priority.  PCT-J was published with the international search report in February 2016. The  international searching authority was the Nordic Patent Institute. Today, 6 March 2017,  Jill decides to enter the European phase before the EPO.

answer_choices.1: One requirement for validly entering the European phase with PCT-J is that a renewal fee must be paid.
answer_choices.2: One requirement for validly entering the European phase with PCT-J is that the designation fee must be paid.
answer_choices.3: For entry into the European phase with PCT-J today, at least one fee for further processing must be paid.
answer_choices.4: For PCT-J the EPO shall carry out a supplementary European search.  Legal questions 2017/P/EN/4

answer_explanation: The renewal fee in respect of the third year for Euro-PCT-J has fallen due earlier, on 31 August 2016, Article 86(1) EPC and Rule 51(1) EPC. For PCT-J, one of the requirements for entry into the European phase today, 6 March 2017 is the payment of the renewal fee in respect of the third year, Rule 159(1)(g) EPC and Guidelines, A-X, 5.2.4. Also the designation fee is due today, since the period under Page 1 of 16 Rule 39 EPC has expired earlier (six months after the publication of the search report, i.e. in August 2016). Note that according to Article 153(6) EPC, the international search report takes the place of the European search report and the mention of its publication. answer_choices.1: A European patent application EP1, for which a reply to a communication under Rule 71(3) EPC was to be filed at the latest on 2 March 2017, and for which the applicant did not file a reply.

answer_choices.4: A European patent application EP4, for which the decision to grant the European patent is dated 6 March 2017.  Legal questions 2017/P/EN/5

Conversely, an application is pending if it was refused and if no appeal has yet been filed until the expiry of the time limit for filing the notice of appeal [28 December°2016 + 10 days (Rule 126(2) EPC) + 2 months (Rule 131(4) EPC) = 7 March 2017], see also G1/09. Thus EP3 is pending until 7 March 2017. For EP4, the decision to grant is issued before the publication of the mention of the grant. question_text: Today, 6 March 2017, Adrienn filed with the EPO a European patent application EP-A.  Adrienn is resident in Hungary. The application documents of EP-A consist of a  description in Hungarian and of two drawings.

answer_choices.1: Adrienn is entitled to a reduction of the filing fee.
answer_choices.2: According to the provisions of the EPC, Adrienn must file one or more claims within two months of filing of EP-A.
answer_choices.3: According to the provisions of the EPC, Adrienn must file the translation of the description within two months of filing of EP-A.
answer_choices.4: According to the provisions of the EPC, Adrienn must pay the filing fee within two months of filing of EP-A.  Legal questions 2017/P/EN/6

One or more claims must be filed within two months of an invitation under Rule 58 EPC to correct the deficiency under Rule 57(c) EPC. A translation of the description must be filed within two month of filing of the European patent application, Rule 6(1) EPC. see also Guidelines, A-VIII, 1.1. answer_choices.2: The appeal fee is reimbursed, if the applicant withdraws the appeal today, 6 March 2017.
answer_choices.3: According to the provisions of the EPC, if the appeal is not allowed within four months of receipt of the statement of grounds, it shall be remitted to the Board of Appeal.
answer_choices.4: The examining division will grant interlocutory revision, if the applicant can convince the examining division that claim 1 of the sole request is novel over D1.  Legal questions 2017/P/EN/7

The appeal fee is reimbursed, if the appeal is withdrawn before the filing of the statement of grounds of appeal (and before the period for filing that statement has expired), Rule 103(1)(b) EPC. If the appeal is not allowed within three months of receipt of the statement of grounds, it shall be remitted to the Board of Appeal, Article 109(2) EPC. If the opposition fee is not paid within the 9 month opposition period, the opposition is not deemed to have been filed, Article 99(1) EPC, second sentence. The opponent cannot remedy a deficiency under Rule 76(2)(c) EPC, such as not mentioning sufficient facts and evidence. In such a case the opposition has to be rejected as inadmissible, see Rule 77(1) EPC, see also Guidelines, D-IV, 1.2.2.1 (v). question_text: A European patent EP-M was granted with only one claim. The claim reads:     “A steel composition M.”    An admissible opposition was filed against EP-M and the ground for opposition is lack of  novelty. The notice of opposition was communicated to the patent proprietor who in reply  filed an amended claim as the main request. The amended claim reads:    “A very thin layer of steel composition M.”    The amendment is based on the description of EP-M as originally filed.

answer_choices.1: The amended claim is admissible under Rule 80 EPC only if the amended claim is novel over the cited prior art.
answer_choices.2: The opponent cannot validly object to clarity of the amended claim, since lack of clarity is not a ground for opposition.
answer_choices.3: The patent proprietor is entitled to file amendments in reply to the communication informing him of the notice of opposition.
answer_choices.4: The current request of the patent proprietor is to reject the opposition.  Legal questions 2017/P/EN/9

answer_explanation: Rule 80 EPC only requires that amendments made in opposition proceedings must be occasioned by the grounds for opposition specified in Article 100 EPC. It is not a requirement of Rule 80 EPC that the amendments actually resolve issues raised in the notice of opposition. Although clarity is not a ground for opposition, in the present case the clarity of the amended claim can be discussed, since the amendment, which was introduced during opposition proceedings, is based on the description (G3/14). The patent proprietor is entitled to file amendments in reply to the communication informing him of the notice of opposition. Since the patent proprietor   Page 4 of 16 requests to maintain the patent in amended form (in accordance to Article 101(3)(a) EPC), his request is not to reject the opposition (in accordance with Article 101(2) EPC).

question_text: The examining division issued a communication under Article 94(3) EPC for European  patent application EP-R. The communication is dated 7 September 2016. The period set  in this communication is four months. On 31 December 2016, the representative for   EP-R fell in a state of legal incapacity and the EPO was informed of it on  10 January 2017. On 12 January 2017, the legal division of the EPO decided to interrupt  the proceedings regarding EP-R. Today, 6 March 2017, the EPO is informed of the  appointment of a new representative for EP-R.

answer_choices.1: The communication is deemed to be delivered on 19 September 2016, since 17 September 2016 is on a Saturday.
answer_choices.2: The proceedings are interrupted with effect of 12 January 2017.
answer_choices.3: After resumption of the proceedings for EP-R, the communication dated 7 September 2016 will be considered null and void and will be notified anew to the new representative.
answer_choices.4: For interruption of the proceedings, no administrative fee has to be paid. Legal questions 2017/P/EN/10

answer_explanation: A communication by the EPO is deemed to be delivered on the tenth day following its posting (Rule 126(2) EPC). For the legal fiction of the deemed delivery, it is immaterial whether the tenth day falls on a Saturday or Sunday. The proceedings are interrupted with legal effect from the date of the occurrence of the event , in this case the legal incapacity of the representative, Rule 142(1)(c) EPC and Guidelines, E-VI, 1.3. The communication dated 7 September 2016 would be considered null and void and would be notified anew to the new representative only in a case where the communication was notified during an interruption period, Guidelines, E-VI, 1.4: this is not the case here. There is no provision in the EPC for paying fees for requesting interruption of the proceedings.

question_text: 26. In the context of chemical inventions and selection inventions, what is the question that arises when a general term in the state of the art is used?

answer_choices.d: Whether the general term used in the citation discloses the subject -matter defined by the special term in the claim or the citation?

question_text: 27. Which of the following is the correct approach for deciding selection novelty according to T 133/92?

question_text: 28. Which of the following is a reason for excluding a combination of alloying elements from patentability under Article 52(2) and (3) EPC 1973?

answer_choices.a: The combination is not a technical process.
answer_choices.b: The combination does not produce a direct technical result.
answer_choices.c: The combination is not carried out on a physical entity.
answer_choices.d: The combination is not described in the prior art.

explanation: According to the text, in the case of an alloy composition, a disclosure of a combination of the different alloying elements within the claimed ranges is necessary for a finding of lack of novelty. Since the different alloying elements interact with each other to form precipitates and solid solutions, their content ranges are not to be considered in isolation but in combination. Therefore, if the combination is not described in the prior art, it is not patentable under Article 52(2) and (3) EPC 1973.

question_text: 32. Which of the following is a requirement for a solution to be considered non-obvious under the problem-solution approach?

answer_choices.a: The solution must be disclosed in the application as providing the solution to the problem.

question_text: 35. What is the requirement for the technical problem addressed by an invention according to the established case law?

question_text: 36. What is essential for comparative tests to be considered suitable evidence of inventive step in cases concerning products such as cosmetics?

question_text: 58. What is the effect of a change in the description or drawings of a patent on the understanding of a claimed feature?

question_text: 138. What is the effect of a party not objecting to the accuracy of the minutes of the oral proceedings as evidence of the course of the proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The minutes are not considered a faithful account of events.
answer_choices.b: The minutes are considered a faithful account of events but can be disregarded.
answer_choices.c: The minutes are considered a faithful account of events and are admitted as evidence.
answer_choices.d: The minutes are not considered a faithful account of events and are not admitted as evidence.

question_text: 139. Which of the following is not a reason for the examining division to reject evidence as late-filed in ex parte case T 545/08?

question_text: 140. When should evidence that the requirements for a stay of the proceedings as per R. 14(1) EPC had been met be provided?

question_text: 141. Which of the following is true about third-party observations in patent proceedings under the EPC?

answer_choices.c: The laws of thought had not been violated

question_text: 144. Which of the following is the standard of proof generally applied by the EPO departments?

answer_choices.d: Up to the hilt

question_text: 145. Which of the following is the correct standard of proof for a public prior use allegation when the evidence lies within the power and knowledge of the opponent?

answer_choices.c: The overall balance of probabilities

question_text: 146. In the context of the public availability of commercial brochures, which of the following standards of proof is considered appropriate by the board in T 1140/09?

answer_choices.d: Strict scrutiny

question_text: 147. Who bears the burden of proving receipt of documents by the EPO?

answer_choices.d: The board of appeal

question_text: 148. In T 862/11, which of the following is true?

question_text: 149. Which of the following is the burden of proof for a party submitting that something has not happened?

answer_choices.c: The EPO must in a case of doubt ("im Zweifel") establish the date on which the letter was delivered.
answer_choices.d: The party can file compelling evidence that the letter was not received.

explanation: According to the text, a party submitting that something has not happened is faced with the difficulty of proving this allegation. The party can essentially presume what could have happened or what normally would have been done if a letter had been received, in order to cast doubt upon the EPO's evidence, but it is hardly ever possible to file compelling evidence that the letter was not received.

question_text: 150. In a patent case, which of the following is true regarding the burden of proof for inventive step when there are contradictory test results?

question_text: 151. Which of the following is the correct order of the principles of interpretation of the Vienna Convention?

question_text: 152. Which of the following is the principle that the Enlarged Board of Appeal of the European Patent Office (EPO) does not apply without exception?

answer_choices.b: The principle of broad construction of exceptions from patentability

answer_choices.d: The principle of contextual interpretation of provisions of the EPC

question_text: 153. Which of the following is true about the relationship between TRIPS and the EPC?

answer_choices.a: TRIPS provisions are binding on the boards of appeal.
answer_choices.b: TRIPS provisions are not binding on the boards of appeal but can be used to interpret provisions of the EPC.

question_text: 154. Which of the following is not a correct statement about the power of the Council to lay down provisions concerning substantive law in the Implementing Regulations?

answer_choices.a: The Council is entitled to provide for issues of substantive law in the Rules of the Implementing Regulations.

question_text: 155. Which of the following is not a board's duty in relation to requests of equal ranking?

answer_choices.a: To give a legal opinion on the admissibility of several requests as guidance for appellants in defining the order in which they would like their requests to be examined.

question_text: 156. What is the principle that parties have a right to have their case decided by?

answer_choices.b: The principle that parties have a right to have their case decided by the judge appointed by the board

question_text: 159. What is the correct statement about a former member of the boards of appeal sitting beside and assisting the respondent's representative during oral proceedings before the opposition division?

answer_choices.a: This is not allowed under the EPC.
answer_choices.b: This is allowed, but the former member cannot make any intervention of his own motion.

answer_choices.d: This is allowed, and the former member can present his case before his former colleagues.

question_text: 160. Which of the following is a requirement for EPO decisions according to R. 113 EPC?

question_text: 161. Which of the following is a reason for a decision to be considered insufficiently reasoned within the meaning of Rule 111(2) EPC?

question_text: 162. What is the correct statement regarding the use of annexes in an examining division's decision according to the case law of the boards of appeal?

answer_choices.d: An examining division's decision should not be supplemented by annexes at all.

question_text: 163. What is the legal effect of corrections according to Rule 140 EPC?

question_text: 168. Which of the following is the correct statement about filing a request for apportionment of costs before the boards of appeal?

question_text: 174. Which of the following is a reason for the EPO to correct the designation of the applicant under Rule 139 EPC?

question_text: 180. Which of the following is a requirement for the exercise of discretionary power by the examining division under Rule 137(3) EPC?

answer_choices.d: The examining division must refuse consent to amend made in advance of any amendment being submitted.

question_text: 181. Which of the following is a requirement for a decision of the EPO to comply with the mandatory requirements of Article 113(1) EPC 1973?

question_text: 186. What is the general rule for retraction of a withdrawal of a European patent application?

question_text: 192. Which of the following is true about the concept of "inadmissibility" in the context of opposition proceedings under the EPC?

question_text: 193. Which of the following is a requirement for an allegation of public prior use to meet the third requirement of Rule 76(2)(c) EPC?

question_text: 195. Which of the following is the duty of an opponent in an opposition procedure according to the EPC provisions?

explanation: According to the text, a complete case must be presented at the start of the proceedings in order to provide the board (and the other parties) with an appeal file that contains every party's complete case and to prevent any tactical procedural abuse. question_text: 216. In appeal proceedings, can a new ground for opposition be introduced if it is unconnected with the reasons given in the appealed decision and is directed only to a new ground for opposition (lack of novelty) based on a new document?

answer_choices.a: Yes, as long as the patent proprietor consents to the introduction of the new ground.
answer_choices.b: Yes, as long as the new ground is within the same legal and factual framework as the opposition proceedings.
answer_choices.c: No, as it is tantamount to a new opposition and is inadmissible.
answer_choices.d: Yes, as long as the patent proprietor at some time responds substantively to the new ground.

explanation: According to the text, an appeal should be within the same legal and factual framework as the opposition proceedings. Therefore, introducing a new ground for opposition (lack of novelty) based on a new document in an appeal unconnected with the reasons given in the appealed decision is contrary to the principles laid down in decisions G 9/91 and G 10/91 and is inadmissible.

question_text: 217. Which of the following is not a reason for the boards to overrule the way in which a department of first instance exercised its discretion in reaching a decision in a particular case?

answer_choices.a: The department of first instance exercised its discretion in accordance with the wrong principles.
answer_choices.b: The department of first instance did not take the right principles into account.
answer_choices.c: The department of first instance exercised its discretion in an arbitrary or unreasonable way.
answer_choices.d: The department of first instance did not exceed the proper limits of its discretion.

explanation: According to the text, the boards should overrule the way in which a department of first instance exercised its discretion in reaching a decision in a particular case only if they conclude that it did so in accordance with the wrong principles, without taking the right principles into account or in an arbitrary or unreasonable way, thereby exceeding the proper limits of its discretion. Therefore, option D is not a reason for the boards to overrule the way in which a department of first instance exercised its discretion in reaching a decision in a particular case.

question_text: 218. Which of the following is not a principle of the EPO's examination of facts in appeal proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The EPO is obliged to examine the facts of its own motion.
answer_choices.b: The EPO may disregard facts or evidence which are not submitted in due time by the parties concerned.
answer_choices.c: The EPO must conduct rehearings of the first-instance proceedings with unlimited right and obligation to look at all fresh matter.
answer_choices.d: The EPO is not restricted to the facts, evidence and arguments provided by the parties and the relief sought.

explanation: According to the text, the EPO is obliged to examine the facts of its own motion, and in doing so, it is not restricted to the facts, evidence and arguments provided by the parties and the relief sought. However, the EPO may disregard facts or evidence which are not submitted in due time by the parties concerned. The text does not mention that the EPO must conduct rehearings of the first-instance proceedings with unlimited right and obligation to look at all fresh matter.

question_text: 219. Which of the following is not a part of a party's appeal case according to the rule according to Art. 12(4) , first sentence, RPBA 2020?

answer_choices.a: Parts that meet the requirements of Art. 12(2) RPBA 2020
answer_choices.b: Parts that were not admissibly raised and maintained in the proceedings leading to the decision under appeal
answer_choices.c: Parts that were not directed to the facts, objections, evidence and requests on which the decision under appeal was based
answer_choices.d: Parts that were not part of the appeal case at the first level of the convergent approach

explanation: According to the text, any part of a party's appeal case that does not meet the requirements of Art. 12(2) RPBA 2020 and was not admissibly raised and maintained in the proceedings leading to the decision under appeal is to be regarded as an amendment of the party's case. Therefore, parts that were not part of the appeal case at the first level of the convergent approach are not a part

question_text: 220. In T 1480/16, what was the board's opinion regarding the deletion of method claims from auxiliary request 5?

answer_choices.a: The deletion was an amendment to the appeal case since it necessitated a new discussion on novelty or inventive step.
answer_choices.b: The deletion was not an amendment to the appeal case since it did not result in any change to the factual situation.
answer_choices.c: The deletion was an amendment to the appeal case since it required a thorough re-evaluation of the matters at issue.
answer_choices.d: The deletion was not an amendment to the appeal case since it did not alter the factual situation and did not require a thorough re-evaluation of the matters at issue.

explanation: According to the text, the board did not consider the deletion of method claims from auxiliary request 5 to be an amendment to the appeal case since it did not result in any change to the factual situation and did not necessitate any new discussion on novelty or inventive step.

question_text: 221. Which of the following is a reason for a factual element to be considered as part of the appeal case?

answer_choices.a: The factual element is apparent from the patent documents on the case file.
answer_choices.b: The factual element is not apparent from the patent documents on the case file.
answer_choices.c: The factual element has been expressly asserted in the appeal proceedings.
answer_choices.d: The factual element has not been expressly asserted in the appeal proceedings.

explanation: According to the text, facts apparent from the patent documents on the case file are not automatically at issue on appeal without having been expressly asserted. This means that a factual element has to be expressly asserted in the appeal proceedings to be considered as part of the appeal case.

legal_basis.text: Article 114(2) EPC and T 482/18 and J 14/19.

question_text: 222. Which of the following is a reason for excluding an objection from being considered on appeal under Art. 12(3) RPBA 2020?

answer_choices.a: The objection is not clearly stated.
answer_choices.b: The objection is not adequately substantiated.
answer_choices.c: The objection is not supported by any evidence.
answer_choices.d: The objection is not mentioned in the opposition proceedings.

explanation: According to the text, Art. 12(3) RPBA 2020 requires that the grounds of appeal contain the appellant's complete case, and that all facts, objections, and evidence relied on be specified expressly. If an objection is not adequately substantiated, it will not be considered on appeal.

question_text: 223. In which of the following cases was the board more likely to admit new lines of attack based on lack of inventive step?

answer_choices.a: The appellant (opponent) had filed the new lines of attack in response to the respondent's reply to the statement of grounds of appeal.
answer_choices.b: The appellant (opponent) had filed the new lines of attack in response to the board's preliminary opinion.
answer_choices.c: The appellant (opponent) had not provided any reasons for first raising these objections after having filed the statement of grounds of appeal.
answer_choices.d: The appellant (opponent) had prevented the respondent from reacting to the attack during the opposition proceedings and the opposition division from deciding on the matter.

explanation: According to the text, the board in T 32/16 admitted a new request in response to the board's preliminary opinion of the objections. Therefore, the board is more likely to admit new lines of attack based on lack of inventive step when they are filed in response to the board's preliminary opinion.

question_text: 224. What is one reason for a request not being admitted during the oral proceedings before the board?

answer_choices.a: The request was filed in response to the board's conclusions that the invention claimed in the main request lacked sufficiency of disclosure and that auxiliary request 8 extended the scope of protection.

answer_choices.d: The request was filed at a late stage of the oral proceedings before the board.

explanation: According to the text, one reason for a request not being admitted during the oral proceedings before the board is that the underlying issues had already been raised in the decision under appeal and/or the communication issued by the board in preparation for the oral proceedings.

legal_basis.text: V.A.4. New submissions on appeal – case law on the RPBA 2020, T 1384/16.

question_text: 225. Which of the following is a reason for not admitting a late substantiated line of attack in an appeal proceeding?

answer_choices.a: The attack had been substantiated for the first time at the oral proceedings before it.
answer_choices.b: The appellant's earlier general submissions on inventive step were regarded as substantiated.

answer_choices.d: The attack would not add complexity to the matter to be discussed.

question_text: 226. In which of the following cases was the board able to admit a newly submitted auxiliary request into the proceedings because there were exceptional circumstances?

answer_choices.a: The board had raised a new objection under Art. 123(2) EPC in its preliminary opinion and the amendments were designed to overcome that objection and did not give rise to any new ones.

answer_choices.c: The newly submitted auxiliary request was filed in ex parte proceedings and the board was able to deal with the amendment without undue delay during the oral proceedings.
answer_choices.d: The newly submitted auxiliary request was filed in inter partes proceedings and the other party had no objection to its admission into the proceedings.

question_text: 227. In which of the following cases did the board see no exceptional circumstances which would justify admitting the auxiliary request into the proceedings?
explanation: In T 2279/16, the board saw no exceptional circumstances which would justify admitting the auxiliary request into the proceedings because the combination of documents on which the board based its inventive step objection in its preliminary opinion was exactly the same as the one which had led to the refusal of the application, and hence this was not a new objection from the board.

legal_basis.text: V.A.4. New submissions on appeal – case law on the RPBA 2020.

question_text: 228. Which of the following is not a reason for the board to admit an auxiliary request filed at the oral proceedings under Article 13(2) RPBA 2020?

answer_choices.a: The board regards it as an amendment within the meaning of Article 13(2) RPBA 2020.
answer_choices.b: The auxiliary request addresses all of the outstanding issues raised by the board.
answer_choices.c: The auxiliary request was filed in response to a case made by the opposing party during the oral proceedings.
answer_choices.d: The board's preliminary opinion in the communication under Article 15(1) RPBA 2020 was changed in the light of the oral discussion of arguments that were all already known from the written proceedings.

question_text: 229. Which of the following is not a reason for the board to consider belated submissions as not justified in T 1904/16?

answer_choices.a: The submissions were not justified by the change of representative shortly before the oral proceedings.
answer_choices.b: The submissions were not justified by the change of the law.

answer_choices.d: The submissions were not justified by the change of the opponent.

legal_basis.text: V.A.4. New submissions on appeal – case law on the RPBA 2020.

question_text: 230. What is the criterion that the boards consider even though it is not referred to in Art. 13(1) RPBA 2020, and cannot be decisive in view of the stage reached in the proceedings and the fact that the new submissions had not been occasioned by any statements made by the patent proprietor in the proceedings before the board or by the board itself?

answer_choices.a: Prima facie relevance
answer_choices.b: Prima facie irrelevance
answer_choices.c: Prima facie admissibility
answer_choices.d: Prima facie inadmissibility

However, it cannot be decisive in view of the stage reached in the proceedings and the fact that the new submissions had not been occasioned by any statements made by the patent proprietor in the proceedings before the board or by the board itself.

question_text: 231. Which of the following is a reason for not admitting new requests at a very late procedural stage (shortly before the oral proceedings)?

answer_choices.a: The requests are prima facie allowable.
answer_choices.b: The requests are unsuitable from the outset to overcome the doubts as to the allowability of the claim.
answer_choices.c: The requests are filed very late (i.e. shortly before or during the oral proceedings).
answer_choices.d: The requests are not accompanied by reasons explaining why the amendments have been made and how they are intended to overcome the objections raised in the course of the proceedings.

explanation: According to the text, the admission of new requests at a very late procedural stage (shortly before the oral proceedings) is only in keeping with the principle of procedural economy if the requests are not unsuitable from the outset to overcome the doubts as to the allowability of the claim. Therefore, the fact that the requests are filed very late (i.e. shortly before or during the oral proceedings) is a reason for not admitting them.

question_text: 232. Which of the following is a reason for refusing to admit new requests filed by the patentee in oral proceedings in appeal proceedings?

answer_choices.a: The subject of the proceedings has changed.
answer_choices.b: The patentee has repeatedly modified its requests until an acceptable set of claims is found.
answer_choices.c: The patentee has taken care not to act in a manner detrimental to the efficient conduct of oral proceedings.
answer_choices.d: The patentee has submitted requests willy -nilly, withdrawn them and then resubmitted them later.

explanation: According to the text, the board in T 1790/06 took account of the conduct of the respondent (patentee) during the oral proceedings. A party's obligations included taking care not to act in a manner detrimental to the efficient conduct of oral proceedings. Submitting requests willy -nilly, withdrawing them and then resubmitting them later was unacceptable, for both the board and other parties. Therefore, option D is a reason for refusing to admit new requests filed by the patentee in oral proceedings in appeal proceedings.

question_text: 233. In which of the following situations is it possible to file a new request after the debate has been closed during oral proceedings?

answer_choices.b: The new request is filed after the board announces its decision, and there is a justification for filing it so late.

The board noted that, once the debate had been closed, the criteria for admitting new submissions were especially strict. However, in this case, there was a justification for filing the new request so late. Therefore, option A is the correct answer.

question_text: 234. What is the correct interpretation of the term "poly" -olefin" in the passage concerned in the application as filed?

answer_choices.c: "Polymethylene"
answer_choices.d: "Polyethylene"

question_text: 235. Which of the following is a reason for not admitting new requests for reasons of procedural economy, even where not filed until a very late stage?

question_text: 236. Which of the following is not a reason for a board to refuse to admit auxiliary requests in appeal proceedings?

answer_choices.c: The requests were not substantiated.
answer_choices.d: The requests were filed during the oral proceedings.

question_text: 237. Which of the following is a criterion to be taken into account by the boards of appeal when deciding whether a late-filed document is admissible in the appeal proceedings?

question_text: 238. Which of the following is a reason for the boards to refuse to include late-filed evidence of public prior use in the proceedings?

question_text: 244. Which of the following is a reason for the board to order reimbursement of the appeal fee in the event of a substantial procedural violation?
